the effect of coupling on receiver sensitivity is not negligible, and should not be ignored.

for the dual polarized receiver to operate at a given sensitivity, the receiver must be designed to be able to operate in the presence of the coupling.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the sensitivity of the receiver is not only a function of the coupling, but is also dependent on the receiver noise figure, the receiver input return loss, the polarization of the signal, the polarization of interference, the polarization of noise, and the receiver polarization discrimination.
coupling between ports of a CP receiver has a significant impact on receiver sensitivity.
the receiver sensitivity of a dual CP feed is a function of both the isolation of the feed and the receiver sensitivity of the individual ports.
